title: Unseeded replay pre-shuffle defeats reproducible training and eval selection
what: ReplayBuffer.flat_shuffled_examples calls Python random.shuffle, but Coach seeds only NumPy and Torch. The generation-seeded DataLoader therefore permutes a different underlying list in every process, and the fixed-seed eval-set indices select different positions. Three fresh subprocesses produced three different orders for the same synthetic buffer.
failure_scenario: Two nominally same-seed A/B arms receive different effective minibatches and frozen eval positions before the treatment acts, adding uncontrolled optimizer and metric noise that can exceed a small treatment effect.
how_to_verify: Run the same ReplayBuffer flatten in three fresh subprocesses and compare order hashes; after the fix, build two same-seed eval sets and assert byte-identical compact_boards.npy and tiny-run checkpoint hashes.
proposed_fix: Remove the redundant Python pre-shuffle and return the canonical flattened list; rely on the already generation-seeded DataLoader shuffle. Alternatively inject a local random.Random seeded from seed and generation. Add an end-to-end deterministic ReplayBuffer-to-eval-set-to-DataLoader regression test.

title: Position-uniform value loss preserves the White-outcome shortcut
what: The buffer preserves games only for eviction, then trains policy and value uniformly over flattened positions with no outcome, absolute-role or phase weighting. A 200-position generation-1 JAX sample had 151 White-win, 33 Black-win and 14 draw rows among 198 role-inferable positions; White-to-move mean v was +0.515 and Black-to-move mean v was -0.684. This lets value MSE fall by learning mover role rather than position quality.
failure_scenario: A role-prior value head supplies biased mixed values for unvisited actions in Gumbel completed-Q at every depth, silently corrupting policy-improvement targets while aggregate value loss and batch win/loss label counts look healthy.
how_to_verify: Preserve game_id, absolute mover, ply and outcome for one current replay export; log minibatch composition and compare the net with colour-only and colour-by-phase baselines using game-cluster bootstrap. On one frozen buffer, compare unweighted versus outcome-balanced value-only loss across at least three seeds while keeping policy batches identical.
proposed_fix: Carry an aligned per-position value weight computed from game-level outcome frequencies, optionally divided by game length; keep policy loss uniform, compute unreduced value MSE, apply normalized weights, and log effective outcome/role/phase composition. Do not rebalance policy targets in the same change.

title: Production Gumbel search has no independent small exact oracle
what: Current Gumbel tests only assert legal support, normalization and completion. There is no pinned non-terminal one-legal-action case, Gumbel terminal-root case, exhaustive short Blokus minimax endgame, or independent completed-Q/Sequential-Halving reference; production bfloat16 is not covered by those exact paths.
failure_scenario: A depth-sign, compact-mask or completed-Q integration regression still returns legal normalized policies and complete games, so all structural tests pass while self-play targets are biased.
how_to_verify: Add deterministic cached forced/pass cases, two-to-four-ply endgames solved by independent Python negamax, and a tiny synthetic tree compared with a NumPy completed-Q plus Sequential-Halving reference; parameterize float32 and bfloat16. The cache already has 40 forced non-pass and 333 pass-only positions.
proposed_fix: Create tests/games/blokusduo/jax/test_exact_gumbel.py using hand-selected cache positions and a local reference that imports no production search helpers. Assert sole-action mass, terminal reward, alternating Q signs, considered-action schedule, chosen action and improved-policy probabilities.

title: JAX self-play PRNG streams are unique and Gumbel noise is per game
what: Generation is folded into the base key, waves and scan plies split it, search/sample/tie streams are separated, mctx splits simulation keys per batch game, and root Gumbel is drawn at full batch-by-action shape. The current backend is single-device. An executed probe found 3840/3840 unique derived keys and 64/64 distinct target rows from identical roots.
failure_scenario: No current failure found. If future pmap or multi-process device replicas reuse the same seed and generation, they would need an added process/device fold-in.
how_to_verify: Retain a regression probe with identical batched roots: assert no duplicate Gumbel/target rows, repeatability at fixed seed, change across generations, and uniqueness after folding process/device IDs when multi-device support lands.
proposed_fix: None for the current backend. For future multi-device fan-out, fold jax.process_index() and replica/device index into the base key before generation.

title: Illegal moves are masked before top-k at root and every child
what: Both Gumbel and PUCT root paths replace illegal logits with -inf before topk_legal, and recurrent_fn does the same at every expanded child. An adversarial probe with illegal logits 1000 versus legal logits at most 1 still returned 64 distinct legal IDs from 414 legal moves.
failure_scenario: No current failure found; illegal logits cannot occupy compact slots unless fewer than top_k legal actions exist, where padding is intentional and mapped to pass.
how_to_verify: Add a regression test with adversarial illegal logits and assert K distinct legal IDs whenever legal_count is at least K, at the root and an instrumented child expansion.

title: Completed-Q and backups stay in the local player-to-move perspective at every depth
what: Terminal reward is from the parent mover perspective with discount 0; every live edge has discount -1; child value is for the child player-to-move. mctx qvalues and completed-Q therefore combine values in the node/parent perspective. A forced three-ply probe produced raw Q signs +0.919, -0.961, +1.000 at depths 0,1,2.
failure_scenario: No current failure found; alternating negamax signs and terminal reward orientation are correct.
how_to_verify: Promote the forced-depth probe into an independent exact test and add short real Blokus endgames as described in CODEX-03.

title: Adam moments, LR clock and AdamW decay have explicit continuation semantics
what: Checkpoints save optimizer and scheduler. Accepted candidates retain moments; rejection restores pre-training moments but intentionally keeps the scheduler advanced; resume restores both; cross-run load_weights intentionally resets both. Scheduler is created once and stepped per epoch. AdamW has one group over all parameters and load_checkpoint reasserts configured decay after legacy state load. Seven focused tests passed; historical optimizer step advanced from 1236 to 129906 across generations.
failure_scenario: No current failure found. Historical checkpoints correctly show decay 0 because those runs predate AdamW; loading them today reasserts the resolved current config decay.
how_to_verify: Keep the existing optimizer/scheduler/weight-decay tests and add an assertion that accepted-generation checkpoint step counters monotonically increase while a rejected candidate restores the exact pre-training moment tensors.
